evidence: The actual frozen workbook Quality Checks!D13 and Internal Quality Checks!D13 require absence of [environment].docker_image while active agent Dockerfile steps exist. Python tomllib parsed the entire frozen task/task.toml; its [environment] section at lines 20-24 contains only build_timeout_sec, network_mode, cpus and memory_mb, with no docker_image. environment/Dockerfile:5-12 actively installs dependencies, :14-15 copies instructions/assets, and :16-23 initializes /app. The Dockerfile matches the frozen template byte for byte. SHA256 values verified against manifest: task.toml=070299982e10ab267fee05b1a312f2247fd23857d8f9baed322528837c4a7e46; environment/Dockerfile=0a75419e9598ded9317b26bbf0d2b12de0b9b11185fb4c9fed1ca7f3e52467d1. Workbook, skill, relevant references and both cited template files also matched their frozen manifest hashes. In-memory adversarial check added docker_image="node:22-bookworm-slim" to the environment section and confirmed detection of the shadowing condition. A conforming alternative using the current Dockerfile FROM directive is accepted: a base image is not a configuration-level prebuilt-image override. Broken product behavior cannot affect this structural check; it is evaluated elsewhere. This row requires source configuration inspection, not a Docker or full judge execution; no such runtime claim is made.
